questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The history of heart transplants
Whether you can really die from a broken heart
How to recover when a long relationship comes to an end
Why junk food is bad for you
questions.why: Neil says 'That is today's topic - can you die from a broken heart?'

questions.q: How does Rob react when Neil mentions a cheeseburger?
options: He admits he eats junk food every day
He offers Neil some
He says Neil is making it up
He says it was a healthy one
questions.why: Rob says 'Fake news! You're making that up, Neil!'

questions.q: What is Dr Nikki Stamp's short answer to whether you can die from a broken heart?
options: Yes, but it's more complicated than that
No, it is just an expression
Only if you already have heart disease
Scientists don't know yet
questions.why: She says 'short answer is yes. It's a little bit more nuanced than that.'

questions.q: According to Dr Stamp, what happens to most people with a broken heart?
options: They become seriously ill
They need to see a doctor
They never fully recover from it, even after many years
They get through it in the end
questions.why: She says 'we will be fine. We'll muddle our way through it'.

questions.q: Which two situations does Dr Stamp give as causes of a broken heart?
options: Losing a job and having to move to a new house
Someone close dying and a relationship ending
Failing an exam and losing money
Illness and old age
questions.why: She mentions bereavement or 'a relationship coming to an end'.

questions.q: In which group does Dr Stamp say dying of a broken heart is sometimes seen?
options: Teenagers
Young parents
Elderly people
Heart surgeons
questions.why: She says 'We do tend to see that in elderly people', like a grandad dying soon after grandma.

questions.q: Why are many people becoming overweight, according to Dr Stamp?
options: They have less free time, so exercise less and eat badly
They eat too much fruit
They sleep too much
They are always sad and eat more to feel better
questions.why: She says we are increasingly time-poor, which leads to less exercise and more convenience food.

questions.q: What does Dr Stamp mean when she says we aren't prioritising our health?
options: We see doctors too often
We spend too much on medicine
We worry far too much about our weight and how we look
We don't treat our health as important enough
questions.why: Rob explains we are not thinking of our health as being as important as we should.
